pages.title: Maui 2010 - 4th of July
pages.summary: Of course the 4th of July has always been a great time to go find some awesome fireworks shows, but I have to say there is something special about watching a show while sitting on a Hawaiian beach with the waves of the Pacific crashing right at your feet!

pages.title: Maui 2010 - Cirque Polynesia
pages.summary: Cirque Polynesia is a acrobatic show (similar to Cirque Du Soleil) infused with Polynesian tradition and flair. Unfortunately, flash and video photography were not allowed so to truly experience this exciting island event you will just have to go see it for yourself!

pages.title: Maui 2010 - Blue Hawaiian Helicopter TOUR
pages.summary: Certainly one of the best way to explore the Hawaiian islands is by helicopter! This time (my wife and I have toured Maui by air before) we decided to check out the area of Maui we were staying in as well as jump over to the island Molokai and it was well worth it! In addition to seeing the cliffs where the entrance to Jurasssic Park was filmed we also saw a couple of manta rays, a sea turtle, and of course tons of gorgeous Hawaiian scenery!

pages.title: Maui 2010 - Maui Ocean Center
pages.summary:
The Maui Ocean Center is an aquarium dedicate to the marine life of the Hawaiian Islands. The aquarium boasts a large array of interactive stations where kids and adults alike quickly learn about Hawaii’s amazing marine life. While you are wondering around don’t hesitate to ask any staff member a question about some of the creatures on display - they love to talk about their current visitors! Of course, the aquarium is one of the best ways to see the beloved sea turtle up close (assuming of course you can’t make it out snorkeling)!

The only media I have of the aquarium is video footage, which takes me a bit longer to process (i.e. cut out all the bad stuff). Stay tuned as I’ll be posting it up here as soon as possible!

pages.title: Maui 2010 - Ocean Sailing
pages.summary:
Without any hesitation or doubt, my absolute favorite activity to do in Hawaii is to get out on a nice sailboat and play in the ocean! For as long as I can remember a trip to Hawaii has always meant spending a good portion of a day (if not the entire day) out sailing. This trip was no different!

Of course sailing in Hawaii spoils your soul! First off, the weather is perfect almost every morning with clear skies and welcoming seas. Second, marine life is overly abundant so you are practically guaranteed to race with the dolphins, swim with the turtles, and see just about every tropical fish you can dream up! Lastly, Hawaii is known for its afternoon winds and being out on the water this is no different. The trade winds that come south down the west side of Maui in the afternoon are the final touch on an otherwise perfect day as your sails fill with wind and you feel the boat being picked up as it swiftly cuts through the ocean.

pages.title: Maui 2010 - The Road to Hana
pages.summary: The road to Hana has lived as a mystery for many people, despite the fact that it is one of the most beautiful drives on the island, the road to Hana has long been known as “off limits” for most tourists due to the extremely poor and hazardous condition of the road. In fact, until recently the rumor was that you needed a Jeep or other 4x4 capable vehicle to actually get all the way to Hana. I’m happy to say that it is now a two lane (occasionally single lane bridge crossings) fully paved and well maintained road that is well worth the few hours it takes to roundtrip.

pages.title: Maui 2010 - Sunsets
pages.summary: Of course a trip to Hawaii can’t be described without mentioning the glorious and unfairly repetitive sunsets! It seems as if every night there is a fire dance in the sky as the sun retreats for the day behind the horizon. The sky takes on an entire new life as night approaches!

pages.title: Maui 2010 - Wailele Polynesian Luau
pages.summary: The Wailele Polynesian Luau tells the story of how Polynesian’s first came to the Hawaiian islands via authentic dances, songs, and colorful costumes throughout the show. Of course a luau wouldn’t be a luau without great food and the Wailele Polynesian didn’t disappoint in that regard, other than at this luau you sit at a table and people bring you the food (not exactly inline with the authentic story line ☺). A great first time luau especially for the kids, next time we will take it up a notch and let her pull some pork off a fire-roasted pig!

pages.title: My Jeep Upgrade
pages.summary: As most of my friends know I eagerly ordered a brand new 2007 Jeep Wrangler Rubicon (4-door model) almost as soon as they were available. I’m proud to say that after almost three years I’ve finally gotten around to giving her the proper upgrades!

pages.title: Sunflower Mine Jeep Excursion
pages.summary: The Sunflower Mine trail is an off road trail in Arizona. The entrance to the trail is about midway between Phoenix and Payson off the Beeline (87) highway. The trail’s highlights are an old abandoned Mercury mine, a creek bed (which occasionally has water running through it), and lots of great camping spots.

pages.title: Madison’s World
pages.summary: This page is dedicated to our daughter Madison, below you will find links to various picture and video albums showcasing her amazing smile and spirit!

pages.title: The Family
pages.summary: On June 25th, 2006 my world forever changed as on this day my family was born! Okay, well born might lead you to the wrong conclusion - that was the day I married my lovely wife Mechelle and her daughter Madison. Below is a little bit of information about them both, as well as links to each of their individual pages. Now, don’t judge me too hard - but I will admit up front that there is slightly more content her about our daughter then about my wife (although I can assure you that is the way she wants it).

pages.title: Noah & Mechelle’s Wedding Photos
pages.summary:
My lovely wife Mechelle and I were married at the Carneros Inn in Napa, CA on June 25th, 2006.

We were honored by all the family and friends who came to Napa to participate in our wedding. Napa of course provided the perfect setting, and the Carneros Inn is one of our favorite spots to stay whenever we visit Napa. I can honestly say that these were the best days of my life.

pages.title: Mechelle & Noah’s Wedding Albums
pages.summary: Below are a number of albums intended to share what is without a doubt the best experience and memory of my life to date - my wedding to Mechelle Childs!

body.text: Below are a number of albums intended to share what is without a doubt the best experience and memory of my life to date - my wedding to Mechelle Childs!

pages.title: Double Musky Express!!!
pages.summary: Below are pictures from a trip I refer to as The Double Musky Express! The trip basically entails collecting up as many of your friends as you can, flying to Alaska, doing some site seeing, and having dinner at The Double Musky - the best restaurant in Alaska if not the entire West coast! Now most folks can figure out how to pull that off without too much trouble, but to do all of that in less than 36 hours is what makes it the Express!

pages.title: 20 Days - Maui Style!
pages.summary: My family and I were blessed with the opportunity to spend 20 glorious days at Ka’anapali Beach on the island of Maui in Hawaii! Our trip was both an escape from the Arizona summer heat as well as a wonderful study in Hawaii living. The best part of our trip was the fact that we weren’t rushed to get anything done, visit any sites, or partake in any “vacation activities” - we had enough time to actually sit back, relax and enjoy our vacation!

pages.title: Park City Ski Trip
pages.summary: Thanks to a good friend of ours my family has access to a great townhouse in Park City, UT. As I’m sure you can imagine, we all love to get out of the sun from time to time and go play in the wonderful snow of Utah! I didn’t get any pictures on the slopes, but here are a few shots from our trip while Madison and I were playing in the snow around the townhouse.

pages.title: Travel Albums
pages.summary: The following albums are a way for my family and I to share with all of you our travels! I hope you enjoy seeing these as much as we enjoyed the trip itself!
